title: ExtExactFunctorCompositionComparison
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal C$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] with small Ext groups [def-pc-ext]. Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, $G:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$, $H:\mathcal A\to\mathcal C$ be additive functors preserving finite limits and finite colimits, and let $e:H\xrightarrow{\sim}G\circ F$ be a natural isomorphism. For objects $A,B\in\mathcal A$, $n\geq0$, and $x\in\operatorname{Ext}^n_{\mathcal A}(A,B)$, let $F_*x$ denote its image under the termwise exact functor on derived categories [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], using the canonical identifications of the single complexes and shifts. For a morphism $a$ write $\operatorname{mk}_0(a)$ for its degree-zero Ext class. Then
$$\operatorname{mk}_0(e_B)\circ H_*x=G_*F_*x\circ\operatorname{mk}_0(e_A).$$

source.place: Lemma Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor), parts (3)-(4), and Definition Tag 06XQ (definition-ext); argument by naturality on localized complexes, written by K1

proof.text: Use the exact functors on derived categories from [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Form the comparison mapDerivedCategoryNatIso e followed by mapDerivedCategoryCompIso F G; the existing library instances show that this comparison commutes with shifts. Expand mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor on single complexes into the factorization isomorphism followed by localization of singleMapHomologicalComplex. Apply mapDerivedCategoryCompIso_fac and mapDerivedCategoryNatIso_fac. The two remaining complex-morphism equalities are checked degreewise: at degree zero the single comparisons are identities and elsewhere the maps are zero. This proves compatibility of the comparison with e on each single complex.

Identify Ext classes with shifted morphisms by [def-pc-ext], using Ext.comp_hom, Ext.mk₀_hom and Ext.mapExactFunctor_hom. Cancel the single-complex comparison isomorphisms to obtain the corresponding inverse-component equality. Apply ShiftedHom.map_naturality to x.hom and the shift-compatible comparison. Precompose with the inverse H single comparison and postcompose with the shifted composite F/G single comparison. Substitute the endpoint equalities just proved, expand the composite functor shift isomorphism, and use commShiftIso_hom_naturality_assoc to obtain precisely the required Ext equality.

lean.statement: theorem mapExactFunctor_comp_mk₀_eq_sheaf {C D E : Type*} [Category C] [Category D] [Category E] [Abelian C] [Abelian D] [Abelian E] [HasExt.{w} C] [HasExt.{w'} D] [HasExt.{w''} E] (F : C ⥤ D) (G : D ⥤ E) (H : C ⥤ E) [F.Additive] [G.Additive] [H.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits F] [PreservesFiniteColimits F] [PreservesFiniteLimits G] [PreservesFiniteColimits G] [PreservesFiniteLimits H] [PreservesFiniteColimits H] (e : H ≅ F ⋙ G) {X Y : C} {n : ℕ} (x : Ext.{w} X Y n) : (x.mapExactFunctor H).comp (Ext.mk₀ (e.hom.app Y)) (add_zero n) = (Ext.mk₀ (e.hom.app X)).comp ((x.mapExactFunctor F).mapExactFunctor G) (zero_add n)
